title: Interlanguage and Mathematical Translation Methodology Sidecar (v0.5 Research Method and Automata Audit)
version: 2026-07-17 v0.5 research method and automata audit
description:
This version extends the interlanguage and mathematical-translation methodology sidecar with a consolidated research method, evidence and authority rules, an operational decision interface, eight language-lane handoffs, and reproducible audits of the current weighted-automata data.

Read first: 00_Interlanguage_Research_Method_Current_v05_20260717.pdf. The grouped file 12_Interlanguage_Research_Department_and_Automata_v05_20260717.zip contains the complete research-department handoff, exact source archives, extracted CSV/JSON/Markdown data, the executable audit, fresh audit results, manifests, and checksums.

Reproduced data state: the Interslavic State C package contains 1,229 ledger rows, 1,215 unique term identifiers, 100 concept buckets, and 9,124 edges. Its W0 result is retained explicitly as a projection only. The unified v6.2 package contains 15 lane rows, 1,522 marker rows, 6,088 edges, and 362 concept rows. Its numerical readiness proxy is reproducible but rejected as a readiness or quality decision measure because candidate mass can produce high scores without accepted witness evidence.

Operational status: this package is research method, reproducibility material, routing infrastructure, and manager handoff documentation. It is not native-speaker approval, community acceptance, a finished interlanguage, a completed translation corpus, or mathematical source-fidelity certification. Generated or candidate material remains distinct from independent source witnesses and accepted terminology.

GitHub: corrections, additional source bodies, improved weighting methods, and cleaned language-lane packages can be suggested through issues or pull requests at https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
notes: v0.5 consolidates the current research method, evidence-governance rules, language-lane handoffs, exact automata data, and executable audit. It does not certify language completion, terminology acceptance, native-speaker approval, translation fidelity, or critical-edition status.
